release_notes.en-US: Uploads without a file dialog: an agent can put files from your computer into a page through an upload button, a drop area, a chat box or a file input, after you allow it on the page (or always on a site you choose). Agents can drag and drop elements, such as cards between columns or items in a list. Big messages from the local program no longer get dropped. The new tools need tether-browser 0.6.0 (npm install -g tether-browser).

version.approval_notes:
Tether is a developer tool: it lets a coding agent the user runs on their own computer (Claude Code, Codex and others) operate browser tabs the user explicitly shares. It does nothing until it is connected to its local program from the open source repository (npm install -g tether-browser, then tether setup). Source: https://github.com/udaysinh-git/tether; build with npm install && npm run build, the Firefox build is dist/firefox; the source is not minified or bundled.

No new permissions in this version. New in it: uploads. The local Tether program reads a file the user's agent names and sends it to the extension, which puts it into a page the user shared, in the page's own world (scripting.executeScript with world MAIN), as a file input's files, a drop or a paste. While one upload call runs (at most 2.5 seconds), HTMLInputElement.prototype.click and showPicker are wrapped so the file dialog the page opens gets the file instead; the originals are restored when the call ends. Every upload first asks the user on the page, naming the files and the site, unless the user turned on bypass mode or chose to allow uploads on that site.

webRequestFilterResponse (since 0.5.0): used in extension/background.js to read the response bodies of fetch and XHR requests made by tabs the user shared, for the agent's network log, and to hold a shared page's first bytes for at most 0.3 seconds until the console hook is injected. The stream is passed through unchanged.

Running user code: the run_js tool, saved scripts and watchers run JavaScript the user's own agent supplies only through the userScripts API (userScripts.execute and userScripts.register), behind the optional userScripts permission the user grants in Tether's settings. There is no eval or Function constructor in the extension. Code comes from the local Tether program on the user's machine, never from a web server, and runs only in tabs the user shared or approved, with an on-page status panel showing Pause and Stop.

nativeMessaging: Firefox upgrades ws://127.0.0.1 to wss://, which cannot reach a local server, so Tether talks to its local program through a native messaging bridge. webRequestBlocking: lifts a page's Content Security Policy only on tabs the user shared, so the user's agent can work there. No data is collected or sent to the developer.
